name: Ryogoku
tagline: Tokyo in 15 minutes and Otemachi in 17 minutes. Served by 2 lines. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥120,000 to ¥130,000.
summary: The station is in Sumida City, where JR East and the Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation run 2 lines between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 17 minutes to Otemachi, 23 minutes to Shinjuku, 33 minutes to Shibuya and 29 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥120,000 to ¥130,000. The station stands 1.9 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 1 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 1.9 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 1 m to 2 m, a difference of 1 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of less than 0.5 m. All nine points within 400 m of the station fall inside the area too, and the deepest projection among them is 0.5 to 3 m. For storm surge, 8 of the nine points also fall inside the projected area. On the whole, the flood projection here is about average for the 23 wards.
medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 9 clinics and 11 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 湘南メディカル記念病院, about 5 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 同愛記念病院, about 7 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 2 lines serve the station. JR Chuo-Sobu Line (Local) run through it. Toei Oedo Line also call here. The lines are split between operators (JR East runs 1 line and the Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation runs 1 line), so when one line stops you can change to a line run by a different company.
congestion: JR Chuo-Sobu Line (Local) runs at 151% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch of the line is 錦糸町→両国, which includes this station. Toei Oedo Line runs at 147% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 中井→東中野, which this station is not on. At 150%, the ministry's scale describes shoulders not quite touching, with crowding near the doors. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥120,000 to ¥130,000 and 1K ¥120,000 to ¥130,000. 1LDK ¥190,000 to ¥200,000 and 2LDK ¥230,000 to ¥240,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.
drivers: Age and construction of the building
Whether it faces a main road or the railway
Whether it sits at the top or the bottom of a slope

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥120,000 to ¥130,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is about average for the 23 wards. For 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: Kuramae is ahead on the number of medical facilities and how easy the shopping is, but Ryogoku is ahead on quiet.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Ryogoku. It reaches Otemachi in about the same time as Ryogoku. One-room rents run about ¥6,000 higher.

neighbours.lead: Asakusabashi is ahead on the number of medical facilities and how easy the shopping is, but Ryogoku is ahead on quiet.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Ryogoku. It reaches Otemachi 4 minutes sooner than Ryogoku. One-room rents run about ¥8,000 higher.

goodFor: People commuting to Otemachi and Marunouchi
People who get around by bicycle or with a pushchair
notFor: People avoiding projected flood inundation areas
noiseSources: The 首都高速6号向島線 viaduct runs a short walk from the station. It is an expressway, so traffic is audible day and night
清澄通り (2 lanes each way) runs just outside the station. In a flat facing it, the cars are audible morning and evening

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: There are 6 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 3 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself sits inside the area projected to flood in the heaviest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: 2 lines serve the station, and the choice of connections is wider than at most stations in the 23 wards.
leads.rentRange: The balance between commuting time and rent is about average for the 23 wards.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is on the high side for the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Morning loading on the lines here is about average for the 23 wards' stations.
leads.noiseSources: The big roads are far enough that traffic noise is unlikely to bother you.
